issues.description: The problem text first instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock field initialized in the constructor (instance-level final initialized at construction), but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute and related methods be static (class-level). This is a contradictory requirement about whether 'stock' is an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static (shared) field. Students could be confused whether to implement stock as an instance final field set in the constructor or as a static field shared across all instances.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification so it consistently states whether 'stock' is an instance final field or a static (class-level) field. If the intent is a shared stock across all saloons, update the earlier paragraph to say 'a static final Stock stock initialized at declaration or in a static initializer' and keep the later note. If the intent is per-instance stock, remove the requirement that 'stock' and related methods be static in the later note and show initialization in the constructor.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares totalOrders as an int ("-totalOrders: int"), but the solution implementation uses a long for totalOrders. This discrepancy in the declared type of the attribute could confuse students about which type to use, especially since the UML explicitly states int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type consistent across artifacts. Either change the UML/specification to indicate long for totalOrders if large counts are expected, or change the solution implementation to int to match the UML. Prefer explicitly stating the intended type in the textual requirements to avoid ambiguity.
